notes.decision: ⲧⲍⲉⲣⲙⲏⲛⲓⲁ = Greek ἑρμηνεία 'interpretation, explanation.' ⲧⲉⲩⲁⲁⲙⲟⲛⲓⲁ = Greek εὐδαιμονία 'eudaimonia, blessedness, prosperity.' Retained as 'Eudaimonia' to preserve the technical Greek philosophical loanword that the Coptic itself uses; the chapter goes on to map worldly Eudaimonia (with worldly Sophia and Dynamis) onto its divine counterpart, the Father in the great land of Light.
ⲧⲟⲁⲙ = Lycopolitan reflex of ⲧϭⲟⲙ 'the Power' (Greek δύναμις). Together with Sophia (Wisdom), these form the worldly triad alongside Eudaimonia which the chapter will compare to the divine triad.

Greek loanword φωστήρ 'luminary, light-bearer.' Standard Manichaean title for Mani himself (the Apostle of Light). Translated 'the Illuminator' to preserve the active light-giving function (per correspondential principle: a title from light-emission stays verbal).
ⲍⲙⲁⲥⲧ = ⲉϥϩⲙⲟⲟⲥ 'while sitting/seated.' ⲧⲥⲁⲩⲍⲉ̄ = ⲧⲥⲱⲟⲩϩⲥ 'the assembly, gathering, congregation.' Standard scene-setting: Mani teaching seated in the Church assembly.

ⲟⲩⲉⲓⲛⲉ here is the verb 'to pass by, transit' (Sah. ⲟⲩⲉⲓⲛⲉ/ⲟⲩⲱⲧⲃ), NOT the noun 'likeness.' Context (the Eudaimonia of the world is transient): 'she passes by/passes away.' The worldly Eudaimonia is contrasted with the abiding divine Eudaimonia of the Father.

Obscure verbal form. Possibly a Lycopolitan compound involving ⲥⲉⲃⲟ-/ⲥⲃⲱ ('teaching/instruction') with feminine subject, or a Greek-derived verb (perhaps from συμβοήθεια 'mutual aid' or related). Tentatively translated 'is paired-with' to fit the parallel context (Sophia is set 'beside' another Sophia in line 27/segment 27, ⲟⲱⲗ ⲁⲍⲁⲛ 'stands beside'). Requires further philological investigation.
ⲟⲱⲗ likely Lycopolitan for ⲱϩⲉ 'stand'; ⲁⲍⲁⲛ = ⲁϩⲏⲛ 'near, beside'; ⲕⲉⲟⲁⲙ = ⲕⲉϭⲟⲙ 'another Power.' Reading: 'stands beside another Power,' the structural parallel to the Sophia clause.

ⲡⲁ-ⲡⲉⲁⲩ 'the one of glory' = 'the glorious one.' The Eudaimonia of the glorious one IS the Father, the God [of Truth]. The text identifies — does not compare — the divine Eudaimonia with the Father himself. This is correspondential identity at the highest register.
ⲡⲛⲁⲟ ⲛⲕⲁⲍ = ⲡⲛⲟϭ ⲛⲕⲁϩ 'the great land/earth.' Standard Manichaean term for the Land of Light, the Father's own dwelling. ⲥⲙⲁⲛⲧ = qualitative of ⲥⲙⲛⲧ 'be founded, established.'

Translated 'the Great One' (or 'the Greatness'). The form parallels ⲧϩⲛⲁⲟ (line 3) where the same root appears with feminine article. Best analyzed as ⲡⲉ-/ⲧ- + ϩⲛⲁⲟ where ϩⲛⲁⲟ is a Lycopolitan substantival form of ⲛⲁϭ 'great' (compare ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲟ̄ 'greatness'). The epenthetic ϩ also appears in ⲛⲉϩⲁⲓⲱⲛ 'the aeons' (line 2), supporting a dialect feature. Functions here as a divine title.

Translated 'again, in turn' throughout. Per glossary, Lycopolitan ⲍⲱⲱϩ = Sahidic ϩⲱⲱϥ (intensive/reflexive). Here the structural function is enumerative ('the X also/in turn') rather than truly reflexive, marking parallel cosmic registers.
Translated 'runs' rather than 'flees.' The Spirit's downward motion through all the aeons reads as cosmological circulation/diffusion, not flight from danger.
ⲧⲁⲍⲙ = Sahidic ⲧⲱϩⲙ 'call, summon, invite.' ⲧⲁⲍⲙⲟⲩ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁϩ = 'they were summoned forth out from him' — emanative-vocative semantics: the divine call brings them out from the Father.

Translated 'the cosmos.' Recurs four times on this page (lines 15, 16, 18, 19) as the spatial domain at the second register, paired structurally with 'the elements' (third register) and 'the Church' (fourth). 'Cosmos' captures the technical Manichaean sense of the manifest world-system.
'The Mind of the Father.' ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲥ rendered 'mind' per mandatory terminology, here functioning as a cosmological hypostasis (the Father's noetic faculty), not the first of the five faculties.
Restored as 'the Virgin of Light' (παρθένος). Standard Manichaean cosmological figure. The fragmentary ending ⲡⲧⲁⲣ at line 18 + [ⲫⲉⲛ]ⲟⲥ at line 19 confirms the reading.
Lycopolitan ⲓⲱⲁⲙⲧ = ϣⲟⲙⲛⲧ 'three.' Feminine 'the third (one),' implicit referent ⲧⲉⲩⲁⲁⲓⲙⲟⲛⲓⲁ = 'the third Eudaimonia' in the enumerative scheme.
Translated 'Might' per glossary. The triad here is Eudaimonia / Sophia / Might (where Might = ⲧⲟⲁⲙ/ⲛⲟⲁⲙ, the third member). Capitalized as cosmic principle.
Tentatively 'those who exist/dwell.' The form is unclear — could be from ⲟⲩⲱϩ 'dwell' or possibly ⲟⲩⲱϣⲙ. Context (the Five Sons of First Man bearing up the All) suggests inhabiting/sustaining sense.
ⲧⲛⲁⲟ = 'the great' (feminine). Restoration ⲛⲉⲩⲁⲁⲓⲙⲟⲛⲓⲁ ⲉⲧⲟ ⲛⲉⲁⲩ follows the page's repeated formula 'their great Eudaimonia which is glory' applied to each register.

ⲛⲥⲁⲍ = 'the teachers' (Sah. ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ). ⲛⲉⲧⲙⲁⲍⲉ = 'those who teach' (Lycopolitan ⲙⲁⲍⲉ = ⲙⲁⲑⲉ from same root). The formula 'leaders and teachers who teach' is standard for the apostolic-ecclesiastical succession; matches ⲣⲉϩ†ⲥⲃⲱ paradigm.

Translated tentatively as 'might.' The word does not match a standard Coptic lexeme; in this triadic 'gift of X' formula (well-being / wisdom / X), 'might/strength' fits the typical Manichaean catalogues of divine gifts. May be a Lycopolitan variant of ϫⲟⲙ ('power, might'), though the orthography is irregular. Recorded as a proposed term.
Read as ϫⲉ ('that, because') + ϩⲁ ('under'). Lycopolitan ⲭⲉ regularly = Sahidic ϫⲉ. The continuation is lost, so the exact construction cannot be determined. Translated minimally as 'that under...'
